decisions.reason: As an older, non-flagship and technically demanding offering, it has likely yielded enough information by 2022 and is more exposed to being culled in favor of newer packaging-wafer options.
This product fits closely with the firm's stated direction in carrier and handling wafers, uses existing capabilities, and is cheap to keep available while demand continues to develop.

Because it was launched as a flagship technology and aligns with the firm's push into multifunctional packaging wafers, management would likely preserve this strategic option despite remaining uncertainty.
An off-the-shelf brand for standard glass and quartz wafers supports the core business directly and has low carrying cost, so there is little reason to withdraw it.

Glass-based circuit boards are a more adjacent bet than the firm's core wafer-substrate business, and after several years without clear strategic emphasis they are more likely to be abandoned to free resources.
